name: Tammuz
title: Pagan Deity Mourned in Jerusalem
summary: Tammuz was a Mesopotamian fertility deity worshipped in the ancient Middle East. In the Bible, Tammuz is mentioned only in the book of Ezekiel, where the prophet sees a vision of women weeping over Tammuz at the entrance to the Lord's temple in Jerusalem. This served as an example of the idolatry that had infiltrated Israel's worship and was one of the reasons for God's judgment on the nation.

keyEvents.title: Women Weep Over Tammuz at the Temple
keyEvents.description: In a vision given to the prophet Ezekiel, God shows him women sitting at the north gate of the Lord's temple, weeping over the pagan god Tammuz. This was one of several abominable practices carried out in and around the temple.

keyEvents.title: Ezekiel's Vision of Idolatry in the Temple
keyEvents.description: The worship of Tammuz was part of a larger vision in which God showed Ezekiel four forms of idolatry taking place in the temple, ranging from paintings of abominations to sun worship. Each abominable act was worse than the one before.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on Idolatry
keyEvents.description: In response to these abominable acts, including the worship of Tammuz, God declares that He will act in wrath and show no mercy. This idolatry was a direct cause of God's judgment against Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The Glory of God Leaves the Temple
keyEvents.description: As a consequence of the idolatry, including the cult of Tammuz, the glory of God gradually departs from the temple in Jerusalem. This was a dramatic sign that God was withdrawing Himself from His people because of their unfaithfulness.

keyEvents.title: Prohibition Against Pagan Worship in the Mosaic Law
keyEvents.description: The worship of foreign gods like Tammuz was strictly forbidden in the Mosaic Law. The people of Israel were repeatedly warned against following the religious practices of the surrounding nations.
